body:
### Problem

```editorconfig
root = true
[foo{1..1}]
```

The EditorConfig file shown above is technically invalid according to <https://spec.editorconfig.org/#glob-expressions>:

> any integer numbers between `num1` and `num2`, where `num1` and `num2` can be either positive or negative. `num1` is required to be ***less than*** `num2`.

(emphasis mine)
But no warning is issued; Vim:E944 is issued when `num1` > `num2`.

### Steps to reproduce

```console
$ cat > .editorconfig << EOF
root = true
[foo{1..1}]
EOF
$ nvim --clean foo1
```

### Expected behavior

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/e04196ea51167924c83850619bbf359665db0d0e/src/nvim/regexp.c#L10649

```diff
--- a/src/nvim/regexp.c
+++ b/src/nvim/regexp.c
@@ -10648,3 +10648,3 @@ collection:
           startc = oldstartc;
-          if (startc > endc) {
+          if (startc >= endc) {
             EMSG_RET_FAIL(_(e_reverse_range));
```

With the patch applied, Vim:E944 is emitted against `{num..num}` pattern (range is not reversed though); possibly it will introduce regression, however.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

e04196ea51167924c83850619bbf359665db0d0e

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

n/a

### Operating system/version

EndeavourOS

### Terminal name/version

ghostty 1.3.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

build from repo
title: EditorConfig `{num..num}` pattern is not rejected
